references.text: The law given to Moses on Sinai, which Jesus referred to when He said He did not come to abolish it but to fulfill it.
Moses speaks of a prophet whom God will raise up, whom the people must listen to, pointing forward to Jesus' role in fulfilling the law and the prophets.
David says that doing God's will and keeping His law is better than sacrifice, which Jesus fulfills through His life and teaching.
Isaiah prophesies about a servant who will bring justice and not break a bruised reed, with whom Jesus identifies and which He fulfills.
Daniel speaks of putting an end to sin, sealing up vision and prophecy, and anointing the most holy place, pointing toward Jesus' work in fulfilling the law and the prophets.
John the Baptist's testimony about Jesus, emphasizing Jesus' role in fulfilling all righteousness.
The author of Hebrews discusses how Jesus is the fulfillment of the law and the final sacrifice for sin, which directly relates to Jesus' words about fulfilling the law.
